one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Scheduled: Q3 2026 results and call on Wed 2026-10-28 (release ~4:05pm ET, call 4:30pm ET) [8]; FCC open meeting 2026-10-29 that may seek comment on making 482 MHz available for satellite-backed coverage [12]; dividend record date 2026-11-25 falls just outside. What I expect from Q3: management pre-guided ~250K postpaid account net adds (vs 277K in Q2) with temporarily elevated churn from the legacy-plan retirement that took effect 2026-07-13 [4][14][15], so a soft account print is largely known; FY26 core EBITDA and the raised $18.4-18.8B adj. FCF guide are likely reaffirmed [4]. The swing factor is tone on Starlink Mobile after the 2026-10-08 Grain 800 MHz deal and the -13.27% day on 2026-10-09 [9][11]; TMUS fell 10.75% on its last earnings day (Jul 23) on churn commentary [31], so the earnings-day move can be large either way. Short-horizon regularities pull in both directions: a 13% one-day drop on a sector-wide, long-dated competitive headline (SpaceX's own CFO targets D2D service for H1 2028 [10]) tends to see partial reversal, but momentum is strongly negative (new 52-week lows repeatedly since Sept [14]) and further SpaceX/FCC headlines are possible. Net: nearly symmetric around $148.58 with a slight upward tilt (median ~$149.5) and monthly vol ~10.5%, a bit above the 33%/3.5 = 9.4% baseline because of the earnings event and post-shock volatility.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at horizon ~$14.50 x 10.5x = $152), EV/EBITDA on StockAnalysis basis (~$37.1B x 7.5x less $117.6B net debt over ~1.045B shares = $154) and FCF yield (2027E adj. FCF $19.5B / 1.045B shares at an 11% yield = $170), weighted 40/35/25 = ~$157.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-10-09 of $14.50 x 10.5x forward P/E (peer median 9.9x, range 2.3x-15.5x; TMUS today 11.8x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Reported consensus figures; I anchor on the lower $13.94.

$13.94 x 1.06. Consensus 3Y EPS CAGR is 17.03% [3]; I use 6% for 2028 to haircut for elevated churn, competitive pricing risk from cable/Starlink and higher spectrum-related interest (C-band 2.0 auction in 2027 [14]).

Peer median forward P/E 9.91x (10 peers, range 2.34x-15.46x); TMUS now 11.82x. 10.5x is a ~6% premium to median, inside the range, justified by 3Y EPS growth forecast of 17.0% vs a peer median of ~7.6% and network leadership (Opensignal 12 of 16 awards [16]); premium kept small because the SpaceX threat makes the durability of TMUS's growth premium the central open question.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM EBITDA (StockAnalysis basis) $37.1B x 7.5x = EV $278.3B; less net debt $117.6B (StockAnalysis, incl. leases) = $160.7B equity / 1.045B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $34.36B x 1.08 (about 4.5%/yr over the ~1.75 years from the TTM midpoint to the NTM midpoint at Oct 2027), consistent with the FY26 core EBITDA guide growing mid-single digits.
Peer median trailing EV/EBITDA 6.9x (range 4.58x-9.72x); TMUS now 8.06x. 7.5x is inside the range, a premium to median for higher growth, below TMUS's current level for the competitive overhang.
Held flat to horizon (judgment: FCF after dividends goes to buybacks and spectrum).
1,072.7M outstanding on 2026-07-17 [6], less ~25-30M net shares retired by Oct 2027: Q2 2026 buybacks were $2.2B/quarter [4]; at ~$150/share and some lower 2027 pace due to the 2027 spectrum auction.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E adjusted FCF $19.5B / 1.045B shares = $18.69 per share at an 11.0% required FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Guidance midpoint $18.6B x 1.05 (mid-single-digit growth in line with EBITDA growth; capex ~flat at ~$10B).

TMUS today: $18.6B / $159.38B mkt cap = 11.7%. Verizon implied FCF = EV $364.34B / EV/FCF 16.92 = $21.5B on $173.05B mkt cap = 12.4%; AT&T = $300.17B / 17.00 = $17.7B on $151.99B = 11.6%. 11.0% is a modest discount to the two national peers for TMUS's faster growth.

bear.story: The SpaceX threat keeps getting more concrete: fast FCC approval of the Grain 800 MHz transfer [9], a terrestrial build or cable/MVNO partner and aggressive Starlink Mobile pricing previews; legacy-plan churn stays high and Q4 or 2027 guidance disappoints. TMUS de-rates to a Verizon-like ~8x on ~$14 EPS (VZ fwd P/E 8.23x [21]) = ~$112.

base.story: Operations keep delivering (FY26 EBITDA/FCF guides met, dividend $4.68 [7], buybacks shrink the share count) while D2D service stays a 2028 story [10]. The overhang fades only partly, so the multiple settles near 10.5x NTM EPS of ~$14.5-14.8, around fair value.

bull.story: Starship/V3 timing slips and experts' view that D2D complements rather than replaces terrestrial networks wins out [12][13]; churn normalizes after the migration, and 2027 guidance plus a new buyback program re-rate the stock to ~13.5x on ~$14.8 EPS (~$200). An extra lift could come from a wholesale or strategic deal with SpaceX (TD Cowen floated SpaceX buying TMUS [18]).

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 2.34x (CHTR) to 15.46x (TU); trailing EV/EBITDA 4.58x (CMCSA) to 9.72x (TU); 3Y EPS growth forecasts -4.5% to +18.0% (median ~7.6%). All StockAnalysis.com at the 2026-10-09 close, so after the Oct 9 sector selloff.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 10.5x forward P/E vs median 9.9x (about +6%); 7.5x EV/EBITDA vs median 6.9x (about +9%). Both are below TMUS's own current 11.8x / 8.1x and inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The small premium rests on structural, measurable differences expected to last through Oct 2027: a 3Y EPS growth forecast of 17.0% vs a ~7.6% peer median [3][21-30]; industry-leading network quality (12 of 16 Opensignal awards vs 3 for Verizon and 1 for AT&T [16]); and FCF still being guided up in 2026 [4]. I kept the premium far below TMUS's historical premium because the main risk, Starlink Mobile's move to retail service with low-band spectrum [9], directly attacks the durability of that growth. Its D2D service is not targeted before H1 2028 [10], so the risk falls mostly beyond the horizon, but it hits the multiple now. Caveat: forward EV/EBITDA was not available from a reachable free source, so trailing EV/EBITDA is used for every peer and for TMUS, on one consistent basis.

thesis_break_reason: $112 is ~8x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.94 [1]), a Verizon-like multiple (8.23x [21]) that would mean the market has fully written off TMUS's growth premium. At that level the likeliest explanation is a real fundamental break, not volatility: postpaid account net adds turning negative or churn staying elevated well after the plan migration, a cut to EBITDA/FCF guidance, or SpaceX securing a terrestrial or MVNO route to scale before 2028 with disruptive pricing. It is ~25% below the current price, about one annual standard deviation at 33% vol, and it sits at my bear-case value.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and call; ~250K account adds pre-guided, churn from plan migration, commentary on Starlink Mobile [8][14]
FCC may seek comment on making 482 MHz available for satellite-backed coverage [12]
FCC review of SpaceX's acquisition of Grain's 800 MHz licenses (SpaceX asked for expedited review) [9]
Q4 2026 results, 2027 guidance, and a new stockholder return program (current $18.2B program runs through 2026-12-31 [4])
Upper C-band (C-band 2.0) spectrum auction, a cash need that competes with buybacks [14]
SpaceX starts launching next-generation V3-based D2D satellites on Starship ahead of H1 2028 service [10]
Expected close of SpaceX's EchoStar 2 GHz spectrum acquisition [12]

key_uncertainties: Whether SpaceX builds or partners for a terrestrial layer (CFO noncommittal [10]; 800 MHz is a coverage rather than a capacity fix per Evercore and Farrar [9][12]) or instead gets an MVNO or wholesale deal; a cable partnership would be the most damaging
How long legacy-plan-migration churn stays elevated and whether account growth (950K-1.05M FY26 guide) holds [4][15]
Multiple path: the stock is a sentiment and multiple story over 12 months, since fundamentals are unlikely to visibly break before 2028
Cash calls on capital returns: the 2027 C-band auction and pricing of the 2027 buyback program [14]
Rates: high-dividend telcos are sensitive to the 10-year Treasury yield
Strategic optionality (SpaceX/TMUS speculation [18], Deutsche Telekom as controlling holder) is unpriced and binary
reasoning: Facts: TMUS closed at $148.58 on 2026-10-09 after a -13.27% day [11]. The trigger was SpaceX agreeing to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz portfolio (up to 14 MHz paired, WSJ-reported ~$8B), which Grain had bought from T-Mobile in Aug 2026 [9]. That came on top of a slide driven by churn from the legacy-plan retirement (up to $6/line, effective 2026-07-13 [15]), a -10.75% Q2 earnings day [31] and further weakness in September [14]. Fundamentals are intact: FY26 core EBITDA guide $37.1-37.5B, adj. FCF guide raised to $18.4-18.8B [4], dividend +15% to $1.17/qtr [7], and consensus FY27 EPS ~$13.94-14.44 still being revised up over 90 days [1][2]. At $148.58 the stock trades at 11.8x forward P/E and an ~11.7% FCF yield on 2026 guidance [3][4]. Alternative-lane evidence: the independent satellite analyst Tim Farrar (TMF Associates) argues D2D complements rather than replaces terrestrial networks, forecasts Starlink Mobile wholesale ARPUs in the tens of cents, and calls 800 MHz too little spectrum without an extensive tower network [12][13]. SpaceX's own CFO pushed D2D service out to H1 2028 and was noncommittal on a terrestrial build [10]. On the other side, VC and social sentiment (Sequoia's Maguire, 2028 as 'the year of D2C' [20]) and Shotwell's roadshow comments on a retail service [19] keep the narrative alive. Alt data is supportive but not decisive: Opensignal's 2026 report gave TMUS 12 of 16 awards [16]; WARN filings show only modest, ongoing cost trimming (647 workers in 2026 [17]), not a crisis; consumer-forum reaction to the forced migration is negative [15], consistent with the guided churn bump. Prediction markets: no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold contract on Starlink Mobile carrier entry or a SpaceX-TMUS deal was found or reachable. 24/7 Wall St reported zero active contracts on a SpaceX carrier acquisition as of 2026-06-25 [18], so no market probability is used. Reddit and X could not be fetched (blocked), and Opensignal's own site returned 403, so its figures come via Broadband Breakfast. Valuation: three methods blend to ~$157 (P/E $152, EV/EBITDA $154, FCF yield $170), only ~6% above the price, because I hold the multiple near the peer median and do not assume a return of TMUS's historical premium. Distribution: scenario mean ~$155 (bear $112 / base $155 / bull $200 at 25/50/25). Ladder uses a roughly lognormal shape with median ~$153 and ~31% vol (realized vol 33%; large-cap base rate +/-25-35%), plus a slightly fatter left tail for a further SpaceX escalation. Thesis break $112. Limits: Twelve Data and some Alpha Vantage endpoints were paywalled. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available, so trailing figures are used. My lane share is below the 60% target: 7 of 31 sources are in-lane, because the mandatory 10-peer comp set (10 data pages), the filings for basic facts, and the trade coverage of the Oct 8-9 event make up the rest. Excluding the 10 peer data pages and 3 filings, 7 of 18 sources are in-lane, and at least 5 (TMF Associates, LayoffTracker WARN data, Droid Life reader reports, 5Gstore market-watch newsletter, SatNews/Sequoia post) are unlikely to be found by other lanes.
